out.other_title: Persuasiveness: an unsupervised debater-strength metric based on judge approval
out.rationale: Like Khan et al., the authors track the relationship between debater skill and judge accuracy, and they measure skill by win rate against other training checkpoints, whereas Khan et al. measure persuasiveness by judge approval and generate a range of expert models with inference-time methods. On this basis EXTENDS fits the method link; the matching result is recorded separately as SUPPORTS.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Method for testing whether an oversight protocol stays truth-seeking under optimization; applies to training checkpoints rather than inference-time variants; Khan et al.'s models are evaluated by unseen LLM judges whose preferences have not been optimized for, while the cited Arnesen et al. passage does not say whether its judge is held out

text: Like Khan et al. (2024), the authors track the relationship between debater skill and judge accuracy on self-play debates, measuring skill as a model's win rate against other training checkpoints. They report a positive relationship for debate, with a 4% absolute increase in judge accuracy after debate training.
title: Like Khan et al., the authors track debater skill against judge accuracy, measuring skill by win rate against training checkpoints
